planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost on the surface of moist mix, since light aids germination; hold off transplanting until nights stay reliably warm.

directions: Beacon Coral belongs to the AAS-winning Beacon series, bred specifically for strong resistance to impatiens downy mildew, the fungal disease that wiped out most seed-grown Impatiens walleriana plantings in North America and Europe after 2011. It forms the same tidy, mounded plant as older impatiens strains but keeps producing its warm coral-pink flowers through humid summer stretches that used to thin out susceptible varieties. Set transplants into consistently moist, fertile, well-drained soil in shade and avoid wetting the foliage when watering. Because it is seed-propagated it establishes quickly and fills in beds or containers with dense color within a few weeks of transplanting.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and keep the mix moist and uncovered, since impatiens seed needs light to sprout evenly.

directions: Beacon Orange is one of six colors in PanAmerican Seed's downy-mildew-resistant Beacon line, developed to bring seed-grown Impatiens walleriana back into shaded landscapes after the 2011-era downy mildew epidemic largely eliminated it from commercial production. Vivid orange flowers cover a compact, well-branched mound continuously from planting to frost without deadheading. Plant into rich, evenly moist soil in deep to partial shade, water at the soil line rather than overhead, and expect noticeably better summer persistence than older, non-resistant seed strains.

common_name: Beacon Violet Shades Impatiens (Downy-Mildew-Resistant Bedding Impatiens)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; transplant into shaded beds or containers once frost danger has fully passed and soil has warmed.

directions: Beacon Violet Shades carries the same built-in resistance to impatiens downy mildew as the rest of the AAS-recognized Beacon series, letting gardeners grow seed-raised violet-purple impatiens without the near-total crop losses that plagued the variety after downy mildew became widespread. Flowers show varying depths of violet across the planting, giving the bed subtle tonal variation rather than a flat single hue. Grow in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in shade, feed lightly through the season, and provide good airflow between plants to further limit foliar disease pressure.

common_name: Fiesta Apple Blossom Double Impatiens (Fully Double Rose-Form Impatiens)

planting.note: Set out started plants after all frost danger has passed into fertile, humus-rich, well-drained shaded soil; Fiesta's fully double blooms are heavier than single impatiens and benefit from a sheltered spot out of strong wind.

directions: Fiesta Apple Blossom produces fully double, ruffled blush-pink flowers with a deeper pink eye that mimic small garden roses far more than the flat, five-petaled form of a typical impatiens. The dense, mounded plant blooms continuously through the warm season in shade to partial shade without any deadheading needed, since spent flowers drop cleanly. Keep the soil evenly moist at all times, since the lush double flowers and foliage wilt fast in dry conditions, and feed on a light, regular schedule to sustain the heavier bloom load through summer.

common_name: Fiesta Sparkler Hot Pink Double Impatiens (Fully Double Rose-Form Impatiens)

planting.note: Set out started plants once frost danger has passed into evenly moist, fertile, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade.

directions: Fiesta Sparkler Hot Pink is part of Ball Horticultural's fully double Fiesta series, prized for saturated hot-pink, rosebud-like flowers packed tightly onto a compact, well-branched mound. It flowers non-stop from planting through the first fall frost in deep shade where few other bedding annuals put on much of a show, and does not require deadheading. Water often enough to keep soil consistently moist, since the fully double flowers and dense foliage are more prone to wilting in dry spells than single-flowered impatiens, and shelter plants from harsh midday sun to protect flower color.

common_name: Fiesta Stardust Purple Double Impatiens (Fully Double Rose-Form Impatiens)

planting.note: Set out started plants after all danger of frost has passed into rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in shade.

directions: Fiesta Stardust Purple bears fully double, deep purple flowers with the same tight, rose-like form that defines the Fiesta series, held above a tidy mounded plant that fills shaded beds and containers with color from spring transplanting until frost. Like other Impatiens walleriana selections, it flowers heavily without deadheading but wilts quickly if the soil dries out, so consistent watering is essential, especially in containers. Provide good air movement between plants and avoid wetting the foliage to reduce the risk of foliar disease common to dense double-flowered impatiens plantings.

common_name: Rockapulco White Impatiens (Fully Double Rose-Bud Impatiens)

planting.note: Plant purchased transplants once all frost danger has passed into moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Rockapulco White forms a symmetrical mound that fills in quickly without pinching.

directions: Rockapulco White is a Proven Winners double impatiens producing clean white, rosebud-shaped flowers over dark green foliage on a naturally symmetrical, mounded plant that needs no pinching or deadheading to stay full. It performs best in partial to full shade in evenly moist, well-drained, fertile soil, blooming continuously from planting through the first fall frost. Like other Impatiens walleriana selections it remains vulnerable to impatiens downy mildew, so provide good air circulation, water at the soil line rather than overhead, and choose a resistant Beacon-series planting nearby if downy mildew has been a recurring local problem.

common_name: Rockapulco Coral Reef Impatiens (Fully Double Rose-Bud Impatiens)

planting.note: Plant purchased transplants after frost danger has passed into moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Rockapulco Coral Reef bears fully double, ruffled coral-orange flowers that resemble tiny roses rather than the flat blooms of standard impatiens, set against a compact, dark green mound bred by Proven Winners for improved heat and humidity tolerance over older double-impatiens strains. It thrives in the deep, humid shade where few other bedding annuals bloom well, flowering nonstop from spring planting until frost with no deadheading required. Keep soil consistently moist and fertile, avoid overhead watering to limit downy mildew pressure, and site it out of strong midday sun, which can fade the coral color and stress the plant.

common_name: Rockapulco Appleblossom Impatiens (Fully Double Rose-Bud Impatiens)

planting.note: Plant purchased transplants once frost danger has passed into moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Rockapulco Appleblossom carries soft blush-pink, fully double flowers with a deeper pink blush toward the center, giving the rosebud-shaped blooms a two-toned effect over a tidy, symmetrical mound of dark green foliage. Bred by Proven Winners for improved vigor in heat and humidity compared to older double impatiens, it flowers continuously from spring planting to frost in partial to full shade without deadheading. Provide consistently moist, fertile, well-drained soil, water at the base of the plant to reduce disease risk, and feed lightly through the season to sustain the heavy double-flower display.

common_name: Rockapulco Rose Impatiens (Fully Double Rose-Bud Impatiens)

planting.note: Plant purchased transplants after all frost danger has passed into moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Rockapulco Rose produces vivid rose-pink, fully double flowers packed densely over a compact, mounded plant, giving the visual effect of miniature roses rather than typical flat impatiens blooms. Part of the Proven Winners Rockapulco line bred for better heat and humidity performance than older double-flowered impatiens, it blooms without interruption from spring through the first fall frost in shade to partial shade. Keep the soil evenly moist and fertile, avoid wetting the foliage when watering, and monitor for downy mildew symptoms since, like all Impatiens walleriana selections, it remains susceptible to the disease.

common_name: Rockapulco Wisteria Impatiens (Fully Double Rose-Bud Impatiens)

planting.note: Plant purchased transplants once frost danger has passed into moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Rockapulco Wisteria offers soft lavender-purple, fully double flowers with the same tight, rosebud form as the rest of the Proven Winners Rockapulco series, held over a neat, dark-foliaged mound that fills out without pinching. The lavender tone is a useful cool-color option alongside the more common reds and pinks of double impatiens, and the plant blooms nonstop from spring planting through frost in shade to partial shade. Grow in consistently moist, fertile, well-drained soil, water carefully at the soil line to limit foliar disease, and site out of hot afternoon sun to keep the lavender flower color from washing out.
